# Independent audit: support minorants and the fixed common-vertex comparison

Audited all five sections of `candidate 24467ade6f021ae8`. Result: **PASS**. No mathematical correction is needed.

The lower support values have the convex Jensen sign: actual Minkowski inclusion gives the target minimum at most the weighted sum of source minima. The displayed Farkas alternative therefore proves a finite affine minorant at every sampled base, including boundary bases and deficient affine rank. No unproved interior subgradient assumption is used.

Substitution of `x=c_p+r_p X` gives precisely the claimed lower margin, with one adjusted base tilt `beta+b`. The comparison source `(r_j-r_p)v+r_pK` has the same fiberwise Jacobian and its anchor centroid is zero. Thus the captured parameter set is contained in the original captured parameter set, with the correct mass inequality. Purely base-normal caps retain identical whole-fiber masses.

Radius concavity follows from ordinary Brunn–Minkowski applied to each actual inclusion. Because the chosen support minimizer v belongs to K, zero belongs to K-v, so nested positive dilations prove all anchored compatibility relations for the comparison source. Its common vertex `r_j v` is fixed across that whole comparison family. The integer-hull assertion is correctly restricted to a lattice-convex support, and does not assert ambient interior at deficient rank.

For a centered simplex, the affine vertex permutation is linear because it fixes the centroid, and has determinant of absolute value one because it preserves the body. The map `A^{-1}(x-r_j v)` sends EVERY comparison fiber to `r_p(K-v_0)` and sends the anchor point zero to `-r_j v_0`. Hence all original normals and all anchors are compared to the ONE fixed source `r_p T` at their corresponding own centroids. Allowing the proof map to depend on the cap and anchor is legitimate: each comparison cap is still bounded below by the same fixed-source depth. This does not assert one global transformation of the original source.

The converse minimization interpretation is valid because the fixed common-vertex arrangement is itself compatible. The stated extension to a vertex-transitive polytope uses the same centroid-fixing and volume-preserving facts. General convex K retains only the directional comparison, as required.

All scalar sums remain discrete, one common continuous marginal law and one common base tilt are retained, and the note does not reduce positive simplex normals to equal or coordinate coefficients. It proves no target depth estimate for arbitrary radius profiles.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
